ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

MAOI transition

A 48-year-old man stopped phenelzine yesterday because of adverse effects. He asks to begin bupropion today. He is clinically stable, and an alternative follow-up plan can be arranged. Which response best addresses the interaction?

  1. Avoid all future antidepressant treatment permanently
  2. Allow the required 14-day interval after the MAOI before starting bupropion
  3. Begin both drugs together at half doses
  4. Start bupropion after a single missed phenelzine dose
  5. Add propranolol and start bupropion immediately
Answer and explanation

Allow the required 14-day interval after the MAOI before starting bupropion

An adequate washout avoids the contraindicated overlap and risk of hypertensive reactions.

Option explanations

Allow the required 14-day interval after the MAOI before starting bupropion: An adequate washout avoids the contraindicated overlap and risk of hypertensive reactions.

Begin both drugs together at half doses: Dose reduction does not make the contraindicated overlap acceptable.

Start bupropion after a single missed phenelzine dose: Irreversible MAO inhibition persists beyond one dosing interval.

Add propranolol and start bupropion immediately: Adding another drug does not remove the contraindication.

Avoid all future antidepressant treatment permanently: A properly planned transition remains possible.
